items.title: Source citations in every episode
items.text: Every line of a script points to the source it came from, and the transcript shows it, so a listener can check any claim. Scripts already carry the citations; next is showing them in the transcript and on the episode page.

items.title: Saved source trays
items.text: Save a mix of feeds and notes as a template that a watchlist refills on a schedule, so a recurring show needs no clicks.

items.title: Longer, smoother episodes
items.text: Get closer to NotebookLM in length and flow, measured in the public [blind test](https://vozonda.com/blind-test/) against NotebookLM and Open Notebook rather than guessed.

items.title: More voice engines, including commercial ones (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, Azure)
items.text: The commercial top voices as engines you can switch on per show, with your own API key, so a show can sound as good as the best voices available today. Local engines stay the default.

items.title: Vozonda Cloud
items.text: A hosted version, paid per episode with Lightning and without accounts, if enough people ask for it. The [waitlist](https://vozonda.com/#cloud) is one anonymous click.

items.title: Hosts with a stance
items.text: Give each host a position on a topic, so a debate is a real debate instead of two people agreeing politely.

items.title: Speaker turns for audio sources
items.text: Know who said what in audio sources: interviews, podcasts and panels are transcribed as turns per speaker, so the script can attribute claims ("the guest argues X, the host disagrees") instead of mixing voices into one block.

items.title: Nostr bookmarks as a source
items.text: Bookmark an article in your Nostr app and it becomes an episode, read from your public bookmark list (NIP-51).
